statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: GHSA-xwfj-jgwm-7wp5 (CVE-2025-58160, RUSTSEC-2025-0055): tracing-subscriber before 0.3.20 writes logged values to the terminal without escaping ANSI escape sequences, so untrusted text that reaches a log message can change what the terminal shows. It is fixed in 0.3.20 by commit 4c52ca5, which adds escaping to the formatter (fmt/format/escape.rs): https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing/security/advisories/GHSA-xwfj-jgwm-7wp5, https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0055.html, https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing/commit/4c52ca5266a3920fc5dfeebda2accf15ee7fb278. Scanned every package of this owner published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: all 17 packages (rust, cargo, rustc-dev, rustfmt, rust-clippy, rust-dbg, rust-src, rust-wasm, rust-uefi, rust-gdb, rust-lldb and the doc and completion packages) of builds 1.91.1-r0, 1.91.1-r3 and 1.91.1-r4, and build 1.91.1-r2, which publishes only rust and cargo. Every file, including the .rlib archives and the .rmeta compiler metadata, was searched for the crate's source paths, which name the crate version it was built from. The compiler library /usr/lib/librustc_driver-*.so in the rust package of every one of those builds, on both architectures, is compiled with tracing-subscriber 0.3.18, as are /usr/bin/rustdoc (rust package) and /usr/bin/rustfmt (rustfmt) in builds 1.91.1-r0, -r3 and -r4, and rustc-dev ships that crate's 0.3.18 compiled metadata for compiler extensions. The published debug symbols (rust-dbg, x86_64 and aarch64, 1.91.1-r0, -r3 and -r4) show tracing-subscriber's default field formatter in librustc_driver and no symbol from the escaping code the fix adds, which the same symbols do show in cargo. cargo is compiled with tracing-subscriber 0.3.20, which carries the fix. No published build of this owner has a fixed copy in the compiler, so every published build is affected.
